output.review_comment: The range check on `p` and the switch to `ceil(p/100*n)` with 1-based rank are correct. They properly fix the 40th-percentile and p90 tests. However, the `if n % 2 == 0 and p == 50` branch that interpolates exists only to make `test_median_response_time` return 135. It contradicts the docstring, which the requester named as the source of truth: "The result is always one of the input values: values are never averaged or interpolated." The README says the same. Under the documented nearest-rank method, `percentile([120, 80, 200, 150], 50)` should return 120 (rank ceil(2)=2), so that test is wrong. The branch also changes production behaviour: the dashboard p50 from `latency_summary` will now show values that aren't real samples when the sample count is even, and p50 no longer uses the same rule as p90/p99. Please remove the special case, keep the validation and the ceil fix, and tell the teammate that `test_median_response_time` conflicts with the documented spec rather than bending the implementation to match it.
